# SCOPE: facility-damage only (named energy infrastructure: refineries, terminals, LNG, petrochem, gas fields, nuclear). Military ops / intercepts / kinetic-without-facility-hit → HAWK domain (LESSONS #3); do NOT log here even if oil-price-relevant.

# ⚑ SCOPE RULING 2026-08-07 (BRENT, own ledger) — THE FLOATING-ASSET AMBIGUITY, RESOLVED. The header said 'facility-damage only' while RF-043 logs an FSRU, i.e. a SHIP — a self-contradiction flagged for 9 days.
#   THE DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT 'IS IT A SHIP?' — it is: DOES THE DAMAGED OBJECT PERFORM A FIXED TERMINAL FUNCTION WHOSE LOSS REMOVES THROUGHPUT CAPACITY AT A NAMED LOCATION?
#     IN  → moored FSRUs/FSUs/FPSOs, SPMs, loading buoys, pipeline-connected floating terminals. They ARE the terminal; hull vs concrete is an engineering detail, not an economic one.
#     OUT → any vessel IN TRANSIT or at anchor as CARGO/TRANSPORT (tankers, LNG carriers, bulkers), however oil-relevant. Those are HAWK's cross-theater STRIKES.tsv, and FALCON's/OSPREY's by theater.
#   ⇒ RF-043 (Energos Winter FSRU, Damietta) is CORRECTLY IN SCOPE — it was a moored import terminal, not a ship in passage.

#   ⇒ AND THE 'BACKLOG' WAS NOT A BACKLOG: GasLog Shanghai (8/1), Velos Amber (8/3) and Minoan Pioneer (8/4) are all vessels IN TRANSIT ⇒ CORRECTLY EXCLUDED, not missing. My own SCRATCH carried them as unlogged debt; under this ruling the ledger was already compliant and the DEFECT WAS THE UNSTATED RULE, not the data.

#   ⚠️ BOUNDARY NOT REDEFINED UNILATERALLY: this narrows MY ledger's admission test only. HAWK owns the cross-theater strike ledger (one table, theater column, no per-theater silos) and nothing here removes anything from it — a moored-FSRU strike can legitimately appear in BOTH, mine as capacity, HAWK's as a strike. Flagged to HAWK via NEXUS_BRIEF rather than edited into HAWK's files.
# ⚑ SCHEMA v2 — 2026-08-13 (BRENT first application of the UNIT/BASIS AUDIT CONVENTION, Will-ruled 2026-08-12;
#   ruling of record PROME/proposals/2026-08-12_audit-convention-RULED.md). 7 columns ADDED, ZERO columns removed,
#   ZERO values changed: capacity_bpd and bpd_offline_est are PRESERVED BYTE-FOR-BYTE as the legacy surface so no
#   existing reader breaks. The new columns are the ones to read.
# ⛔ THE STANDING VERDICT THIS SCHEMA DOES NOT REPEAL (Will-ruled fleet-wide 2026-08-12, from BRENT's own audit):
#   NO AGGREGATE OVER THIS FILE IS QUOTABLE. It is an EVENT RECORD, not a CAPACITY MEASURE. The unit columns make
#   the units VISIBLE; they do not make the file summable. Six of these rows are not denominated in barrels at all.
# NEW COLUMNS
#   facility_key      normalized <COUNTRY>:<FACILITY> identity. EXISTS SO RE-STRIKES COLLIDE MECHANICALLY (I-6) —
#                     before this, exact-name matching found ZERO repeat-struck facilities while token matching
#                     found 6 groups, i.e. no mechanical check could ever detect a re-strike. Repeat groups today:
#                     IRN:KHARG_ISLAND (RF-002/RF-019) · MEX:DOS_BOCAS (RF-003/RF-020) ·
#                     RUS:CPC_MARINE_TERMINAL (RF-038/RF-042) · SAU:JAZAN (RF-039/RF-044).
#   capacity_unit     unit for capacity_qty      | BPD · MTPA · BCFD · MW · PCT_EXPORTS · STORAGE
#   capacity_qty      quantity IN capacity_unit  (blank when the state says there is no number)
#   capacity_state    value vocabulary, below
#   offline_unit      unit for offline_qty
#   offline_qty       quantity IN offline_unit   (blank when the state says there is no number)
#   offline_state     value vocabulary, below
# ⚑ VALUE VOCABULARY — the whole point of the ruling: ZERO, UNKNOWN and NOT-APPLICABLE must be DISTINGUISHABLE.
#   Before this migration one token `0` carried FOUR meanings and `blank` a fifth, in TWO columns, with no key —
#   so a naive sum read 13 blank rows (the entire August Russian strike wave) as zero barrels offline.
#     MEASURED            a real measured number, including a genuine measured 0
#     ZERO-RESTORED       0 because the facility was restored / the incident RESOLVED
#     ZERO-INTACT         0 because nothing was damaged — attacked-and-spared, or a watch row with no loss
#     ZERO-NODOUBLECOUNT  DELIBERATELY 0: the barrels are already counted on an earlier row for the same
#                         facility_key. ⚠️ NEVER 'fix' one of these by filling in a number — that is the
#                         double-count the convention exists to prevent (latent hazard: RF-042 CPC, 1.3M bpd).
#     UNKNOWN             bpd IS the right unit and nobody has ever measured it. NOT zero.
#     DERIVED-BOUND       ⚑ ADDED 2026-08-21. The number is an UPPER BOUND computed from a published PERCENTAGE-OF-CAPACITY
#                         statement, not a measured outage. Operators overwhelmingly disclose restarts as '>90% of capacity',
#                         never as a bpd-offline figure, so this state is the normal one after a partial restart.
#                         ⛔ MEASURED would have been a lie and UNKNOWN would have thrown away a real bound — the field existed
#                         to record HOW WE KNOW, and neither existing token could say 'bounded by arithmetic on the operator's own figure'.
#                         ✅ SAFE TO ADD: offline_state has NO programmatic reader (verified by grep across the repo) — it is a
#                         documentation field, and I-8 filters on capacity_unit/offline_unit, not on this column.
#                         ⚠️ TREAT AS A CEILING, NEVER A POINT ESTIMATE, and never sum these with MEASURED values as if alike.
#     NA-WRONG-UNIT       the asset is REAL but is not denominable in this column's unit — read capacity_unit/qty
#                         for the true figure (LNG in MTPA, gas in BCFD, nuclear in MW, a terminal in % of exports).
#     UNLOGGED            blank: no figure was ever published or attempted. NOT zero, NOT unknown-after-looking.
#   HISTORICAL DISTRIBUTION (2026-08-13, not re-certified by cleanup):
#     capacity_state  MEASURED 39 · UNLOGGED 7 · NA-WRONG-UNIT 6 · UNKNOWN 1
#     offline_state   MEASURED 19 · UNLOGGED 13 · ZERO-RESTORED 10 · NA-WRONG-UNIT 4 · ZERO-INTACT 4 ·
#                     ZERO-NODOUBLECOUNT 2 · UNKNOWN 1
# ⚠️ SEAM DECLARED, NOT HIDDEN: DAEDALUS owns the fleet token encode (STATE_VOCABULARY.md). As of 2026-08-13 that
#   file carries Classes 1-4 (banners / gates / predictions / queue) and has NO class for the zero-vs-unknown-vs-
#   not-applicable distinction, so these are BRENT-LOCAL TOKENS chosen under PROME's explicit instruction to use
#   my own and flag the seam rather than wait. IF DAEDALUS'S CANONICAL SPELLINGS DIFFER, THIS FILE RENAMES TO
#   MATCH — the distinctions are the ruling, the spellings are not.
# ⚑ COVERAGE (I-3, 2026-08-13) — states what this ledger CLAIMS to be complete for, so a reader can tell
#   'no events occurred' from 'nobody logged'. Before this line the file could not distinguish them.
#   HISTORICAL COVERAGE CLAIM (not re-certified 2026-09-08): 2026-03-02 -> 2026-08-10 for facility-damage events meeting the SCOPE test below.
#   ⚑ 2026-06 = VERIFIED QUIET, NOT UNLOGGED. Zero rows in June and the longest inter-event gap in the file is
#     2026-05-17 -> 2026-07-12 = 56 days. PROBED, not assumed: June 2026 was the de-escalation window (Islamabad

#     facility-damage events surfaced NONE. ⇒ the gap is believed REAL. [[finding_verification_zero_is_ambiguous]]
#   ⛔ KNOWN INCOMPLETE beyond the claimed window: the Novorossiysk / Sheskharis strike of 2026-08-11-12 is NOT

TWO ROWS ON ONE FACILITY ASSERTED OPPOSITE THINGS FOR ~4 MONTHS and nothing could see it, because before today the ledger had no facility identifier and exact-name matching found ZERO repeat-struck facilities. The schema change caught a live contradiction on its first working day. || ⚠️ THE BARRELS ARE GENUINELY OFFLINE TODAY - BUT FOR AN OUT-OF-SCOPE REASON, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT: Kharg has been IDLE since ~2026-07-31 under a US NAVAL BLOCKADE (satellite: all three terminals empty on 8/1, western vacant 14 days; 16-19 dark-signal tankers in the waiting area). A BLOCKADE IS A MILITARY OPERATION, NOT FACILITY DAMAGE, and this ledger's SCOPE header restricts it to facility damage with military ops routed to HAWK. ⇒ recording it here as damage-offline would double-count HAWK's ledger AND misattribute a commercial/access constraint to physical destruction. ROUTED TO HAWK rather than logged here. || NET: zero facility damage at Kharg on the current record; the export loss is real, is somebody else's row, and is NOT a capacity write-down.

I CANNOT date its restoration, and I have NO ADNOC operator statement - the source is a regional outlet relaying trade-flow trackers. ⛔ TWO SOURCES DELIBERATELY REFUSED AS EVIDENCE: GEM's 'Status: Operating' field is a PROJECT-LIFECYCLE value (operating vs construction vs cancelled), NOT a real-time outage flag, and Wikipedia carries only the 2012 commissioning - neither is an instrument for this question ([[finding_guidance_is_not_the_instrument]]). || ⛔ AND THE ROW WAS PROBABLY WRONG WHEN WRITTEN, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL FINDING: the logged event is a PUMPING-STATION FIRE (2026-03-30, incident_type PIPELINE_PUMPING_FIRE) and the row assigned the FULL NAMEPLATE 1.5M as offline on source_tier A-2 with 'UAE has not attributed cause'. A working bypass means BARRELS THROUGH THE STRAIT != BARRELS LOST, so a low PortWatch transit count means materially LESS than my surfaces have implied.
